name: Cosmetic limb lengthening in India

lead: Cosmetic limb lengthening is an orthopedic procedure in which the thigh or shin bones are cut and slowly stretched apart so new bone forms in the gap, adding height. In India it is offered to people of normal stature who want to be taller, and the country has become one of the places height seekers consider for it.

The technique descends from distraction osteogenesis, developed for limb-length differences and deformities. Surgeons' case reports and news coverage describe gains in the range of several centimeters, alongside a recovery that lasts many months.

paras: Patients typically undergo an operation to cut the bone and fit either an external frame or an internal lengthening nail, then lengthen the limb gradually by about a millimeter a day, followed by a consolidation period while the bone hardens and a second operation to remove hardware. Physiotherapy runs through the process.

Reported problems include infection, nonunion or malalignment of the bone, hardware failure, nerve injury, pain and the need for further surgery. Press reports from India describe patients who gained less height than expected and others who said they were not fully informed of risks, and the sector has been described as lightly regulated. Medical groups in several countries recommend discussing the procedure with a qualified limb-reconstruction surgeon.

angle.text: The procedure lengthens the leg bones themselves, so the added height is permanent rather than worn. People pursue it to be taller in daily life, citing social and career reasons. It takes months of lengthening and recovery.

lead: Cosmetic limb lengthening in India refers to elective surgery, offered by orthopedic clinics there, that increases the height of people who have no growth disorder by lengthening the femur, tibia or both. Practitioners and patients present it as a way to gain height that other methods, such as lifts, cannot permanently give. [1]

The surgery uses distraction osteogenesis: the surgeon cuts the bone, waits roughly a week, then separates the pieces at about a millimeter per day so new bone fills the gap, after which the bone consolidates and the hardware is removed or retained. [1] The method was first used clinically for unequal leg length; Wikipedia traces the idea to Bernhard von Langenbeck in 1869, an early clinical report by Alessandro Codivilla in 1905, and Gavriil Ilizarov's work in the 1950s that made the approach widespread. [1]

According to Wikipedia's summary of media reports, cosmetic lengthening is in high demand in India and unregulated, with patients citing marriage and career prospects and plans to work abroad. [1] The same account notes reports of very young patients, infections requiring further surgery, lower-than-expected gains, and a surgeon criticizing short fellowships as the training some practitioners have. [1]
infobox: Distraction osteogenesis (external frame or internal nail)

paras: The operation cuts the bone, usually the femur or tibia, and uses a device to pull the ends apart slowly. Manual frames, rod systems and motorized fully implantable nails such as the Fitbone are described in the literature. [1] Wikipedia notes that going too fast risks nonunion while too slow risks premature union. [1]

Wikipedia reports that height is seen as attractive in India and that cosmetic lengthening has grown there, with some young people using it to improve marriage and career prospects or to prepare for jobs overseas. [1] Clinics advertise to domestic and international patients, and the cost advantage over Western clinics is a commonly cited draw in coverage of height surgery.

General complication rates from distraction osteogenesis include infection (about 5%), growth in an unintended direction, hardware failure and nerve injury, according to the Wikipedia summary, which is mostly based on jaw lengthening. [1] Reports specific to India describe infections needing more surgery, smaller gains than promised and patients who say risks were understated. [1] China banned cosmetic limb lengthening in 2006 after a series of operations with serious side effects. [1]

No studies found specifically on cosmetic limb lengthening in India. Distraction osteogenesis for limb-length discrepancy and deformity is well documented in the orthopedic literature, but those studies concern medical indications rather than elective height gain.
